title: Calcium Imaging of Dorsal and Ventral CA1 Neurons in Mice
author: Yun, Shin, et al.
materials: eye lubricant (Optixcare Pet Eye Lube Plus)

Drug concentrations may differ between brands. Dilute as necessary.•Lidocaine solution: Mix 2.5 mL of 2% lidocaine hydrochloride hydrate (21.33 mg/mL) and 2.5 mL of bupivacaine (5 mg/mL), dilute the mixture with 5 mL of saline at 25°C, aliquot it into 0.5 mL volumes, and store at 4°C.•Ketoprofen solution: Mix 2 mL of ketoprofen (50 mg/mL) and 98 mL of saline at 25°C, aliquot it into 0.5 mL volumes, and store at 4°C.•Chlorhexidine gluconate solution: Mix 100 mL of chlorhexidine gluconate solution (0.25 mL/mL) and 900 mL of 70% ethanol at 25°C, and store at 4°C.
This study did not generate any new unique reagents.

steps.title: Prepare and sterilize instruments
steps.instruction: Gather eye lubricant, stainless steel bowl, saline, 3M Vetbond, lidocaine, ketoprofen, chlorhexidine solution, Kwik‑Cast, Kwik‑Sil, forceps, surgical scissors, 0.5 mm drill bit, 1 mL syringe, insulin syringe, 26 G needle, 5‑0 monocryl suture, Cutanplast, cotton swabs. Autoclave scissors, forceps, and swabs; keep all items soaked in chlorhexidine when not in use.

steps.title: Dilute viral stock
steps.instruction: In a pipette tube place the AAV1‑CamKII‑GCaMP6f‑WPRE‑SV40 viral stock, add saline to reach a final concentration of 2 × 10¹² vg · mL⁻¹. Dispense 3 µL of this diluted virus into each PCR tube and store the remaining diluted virus at –83 °C.

steps.title: Pull glass injection pipettes
steps.instruction: Load a 1.0 mm OD / 0.75 mm ID borosilicate capillary onto the vertical micropipette puller. Pull with Temperature = 62 °C, weight = ‘heavy 1’, pull‑position plate = 5 mm. Cut the tip with surgical scissors so the final tip diameter is <0.0035 mm and the thin segment is >1 cm long.

steps.title: Set up virus injection system
steps.instruction: Connect a Hamilton 75 RN syringe to the pulled glass pipette using a Hamilton RN compression fitting. Fill the syringe with mineral oil, mount it on the syringe pump, and verify smooth operation.

steps.title: Assemble suction apparatus
steps.instruction: Use a suction pump capable of >50 kPa, an 8 mm‑diameter hose, a 1 mL syringe and a 24 G needle. Cut the needle to make a flat‑ended suction needle, connect one hose end to the pump and the other to the syringe barrel, and optionally seal joints with Teflon tape. Attach the suction needle to the syringe.

steps.title: Construct dorsal lens holder
steps.instruction: Cut a P200 tip at 24.5 mm, 27 mm and 45 mm from the narrow end; keep the 0–24.5 mm and 27–45 mm segments. Cut a P1000 tip at 2 mm and 27 mm; keep the 2–27 mm segment. Glue the 0–24.5 mm P200 segment into the 27–45 mm P200 segment, then glue the P1000 segment over the narrow ends leaving a 1 mm gap. Connect a 4 mm‑diameter hose to the narrow end of the assembled tip, attach a 1 mm syringe parallel to the stereotaxic holder with glue and labeling tape, and join the tip assembly to the syringe from the suction setup.

steps.title: Construct ventral lens holder
steps.instruction: Secure a stainless‑steel M1.4 × 40–60 mm threaded rod with two M1.4 × 1 mm nuts to a custom 1 mm‑thick aluminum holder using Loctite 401 (optional Kwik‑Sil wrap). Insert a 0.6 × 7.3 mm GRIN lens into the holder’s smallest hole so at least 5 mm of the lens bottom protrudes, then glue the lens in place with Loctite 401 using a 24 G needle.

steps.title: Prepare head plate
steps.instruction: Obtain a 1 mm‑thick customized aluminum head holder for later fixation.

steps.title: Prepare drug solutions
steps.instruction: Lidocaine: mix 2.5 mL of 2 % lidocaine HCl (21.33 mg · mL⁻¹) with 2.5 mL bupivacaine (5 mg · mL⁻¹), add 5 mL saline (25 °C), aliquot 0.5 mL, store at 4 °C. Ketoprofen: mix 2 mL ketoprofen (50 mg · mL⁻¹) with 98 mL saline (25 °C), aliquot 0.5 mL, store at 4 °C. Chlorhexidine: mix 100 mL 0.25 mL · mL⁻¹ chlorhexidine gluconate with 900 mL 70 % ethanol, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Place mouse in induction chamber, deliver 3 % isoflurane at 1 L · min⁻¹. Confirm anesthesia by relaxed body/tail, gasping ~1 s⁻¹, and no response to toe pinch (≈5 min).

steps.title: Mount mouse in stereotaxic
steps.instruction: Fit mouse nose into a mask supplying 3 % isoflurane, secure head with ear bars, set homeothermic system to 33.5 °C.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Disinfect scalp with chlorhexidine, trim hair, re‑disinfect, dab ~100 µL lidocaine solution, inject ketoprofen IM (100 µL · g⁻¹), make a 1.2 cm midline incision, apply eye lubricant.

steps.title: Clean skull
steps.instruction: Widen incision with sterile cotton swabs, clean exposed skull with dry swab then saline‑dipped swab.

steps.title: Level skull
steps.instruction: Attach a 22–26 G needle to the stereotaxic holder, ink tip, touch bregma and lambda, measure DV difference, adjust dorsal/ventral dial until the bregma‑lambda difference is <0.02 mm.

steps.title: Mark dorsal CA1 site
steps.instruction: Mark a point 1.94 mm posterior to bregma, then 1.40 mm lateral from that point. From this target, mark four peripheral points 0.60 mm anterior, posterior, medial and lateral.

steps.title: Drill dorsal skull hole
steps.instruction: Mount the 0.5 mm drill bit on a micro‑hand drill and create a square opening ≈1.2 mm on each side within the peripheral marks, taking care not to tear dura.

steps.title: Inject virus dorsal CA1
steps.instruction: Load Hamilton syringe with 1 µL of diluted virus. For site 1 (1.94 mm posterior, 1.15 mm lateral) and site 2 (1.94 mm posterior, 1.60 mm lateral), lower syringe to 1.1 mm depth (0.05 mm above target), wait 5 min, inject 0.4 µL at 0.05 µL · min⁻¹ (8 min total). Verify volume decrease; if not, clear tip with saline‑soaked Cutanplast or recut tip. After each injection wait 10 min, then retract syringe.

steps.title: Seal injection site
steps.instruction: Blend Kwik‑Sil, fill the drilled hole, wait 3 min for setting.

steps.title: Suture and recover
steps.instruction: Place suture needle through skin on both sides, tie knots until skin is closed. Allow 2 weeks for viral expression before the next surgery.

steps.title: Incise skin for lens implantation
steps.instruction: Make an isosceles trapezoid incision: a short cut along the ear‑bar line between the eyes, oblique cuts toward each inner eye corner, and a cut near the eyes. Apply 3M Vetbond along the cut to attach skin to skull.

steps.title: Attach head plate
steps.instruction: Soak head plate and screws in chlorhexidine, align head plate slightly anterior to coronal suture, drill shallow indentations (<1 mm deep) beneath each screw hole and one above cerebellum, then secure screws with a screwdriver.

steps.title: Aspirate cortical tissue
steps.instruction: Remove Kwik‑Sil from the previous hole, set up suction apparatus, turn pump to >50 kPa, aspirate cortex until white corpus callosum appears, intermittently apply saline with an insulin syringe to keep view clear. Stop when corpus callosum is visible, turn off pump, absorb blood with saline‑soaked Cutanplast, replace Cutanplast if needed, ensure bleeding stops.

steps.title: Implant dorsal GRIN lens
steps.instruction: Sterilize a 1.0 × 4.0 mm GRIN lens with chlorhexidine. Fix dorsal lens holder to stereotaxic holder, turn suction pump on (>50 kPa), load lens onto tip assembly, align lens centre to the reference point (1.94 mm posterior, 1.40 mm lateral). Lower lens to just above skull, then to 0.7 mm below that point rapidly, then lower an additional 1.0 mm at 0.2 mm · min⁻¹ to reach 1.7 mm below the reference. Stop if bleeding occurs, absorb with Cutanplast, then resume.

steps.title: Cement dorsal lens
steps.instruction: Cover lens, skull, head plate and screws with Super Bond C&B; avoid covering the tip assembly. After cement hardens, switch off suction, disconnect holder, optionally add extra dental cement to exposed areas. Wait ≥10 min for cement to harden.

steps.title: Protect dorsal lens
steps.instruction: Apply Kwik‑Cast over the lens, then cover the upper cement surface with Kwik‑Sil.

steps.title: Stabilize dorsal implant
steps.instruction: Allow 1–2 weeks for the cement to fully harden and the implant to stabilize before imaging.

steps.title: Mark ventral CA1 site
steps.instruction: Mark a point 3.16 mm posterior to bregma, then 3.50 mm lateral from that point. From this target, mark four peripheral points 0.60 mm away in anterior, posterior, medial and lateral directions.

steps.title: Drill ventral skull hole
steps.instruction: Using the same drill bit, create a square opening ≈0.8 mm on each side within the peripheral marks.

steps.title: Inject virus ventral CA1
steps.instruction: Load Hamilton syringe with diluted virus, position over two sites (3.16 mm posterior, 3.5 mm lateral; depth 3.5 mm and 3.7 mm ventral). Inject 0.3 µL at 0.05 µL · min⁻¹ (≈6 min per site). Wait 10 min after each injection for spread.

steps.title: Attach head plate ventral
steps.instruction: Before tightening, verify that the lens holder, head plate and screws are positioned so they do not obstruct each other; place the additional screw in a location different from the dorsal surgery. Then repeat the head‑plate attachment procedure as in step 12.

steps.title: Position ventral lens
steps.instruction: Mount the ventral lens holder onto the stereotaxic holder, align the 0.6 × 7.3 mm GRIN lens to 3.16 mm posterior and 3.50 mm lateral to bregma, and verify parallelism with the skull.

steps.title: Lower ventral lens
steps.instruction: Lower the lens by 0.2 mm every 2 min until 2.0 mm below brain surface, then 0.1 mm every 2 min to 3.0 mm, finally 0.05 mm every 2 min to 3.6 mm. Stop immediately if bleeding appears, absorb with Cutanplast, wait for hemostasis, then continue.

steps.title: Cement ventral lens
steps.instruction: Cover lens, head plate and screws with Super Bond C&B, covering the first two holes of the lens holder but leaving the third hole open. Cut the third hole with nippers (posterior side first, then anterior) being careful not to damage the lens. Apply dental cement over the cut holder and any exposed skull, let harden ≥10 min.

steps.title: Protect ventral lens
steps.instruction: Apply Kwik‑Cast and Kwik‑Sil over the ventral lens as done for the dorsal implant.

steps.title: Stabilize ventral implant
steps.instruction: Wait 3–4 weeks for viral expression and cement hardening before imaging.

steps.title: Mount baseplate and microscope
steps.instruction: Remove Kwik‑Cast and Kwik‑Sil with forceps, wipe lens with 70 % ethanol‑soaked cotton. Set up the nVista system, attach the Inscopix microscope to the baseplate, lower the microscope over the lens, reduce isoflurane to 1 % and adjust focus until neurons are clearly visible; mark this position. Surround the lens with black cement or black manicure, avoiding contact with the lens surface. Build a UV‑resin foundation on the underside of the baseplate, cure with a UV beam, repeat resin application until the foundation reaches the height of the baseplate, reinforce gaps with additional resin, verify focus has not shifted, then cover the exterior of the foundation with black manicure. Finally, place the protective cover over the baseplate.

description: The majority of physiological studies in rodents have targeted the dorsal, rather than ventral, hippocampus because the latter region is located deep in the brain, making it difficult to identify the cell body layer with an electrode. Calcium imaging, which enables visualization of target neurons, alleviates this problem. We recently compared neuronal activity in the dorsal and ventral hippocampus using one-photon calcium imaging.1 The following protocol describes procedures for imaging calcium signals from pyramidal cells expressing GCaMP6f proteins2 in the dorsal and ventral CA1 regions. The protocol’s main goals are to maximize cell yield and field of view stability. Drawings of the head plate used for head fixation as well as two different lens holders used to implant a GRIN lens in the dorsal and ventral CA1 are included.
